panels.title: Executed-test pass rate
panels.description:
This is NOT the bench generation gate. It measures whether the generated Robot test passed when it ran, over whatever range the dashboard time picker is set to — narrowing the range changes this number. Spine is execution_records; timestamp is TEXT holding UTC values in two shapes (verified 2026-08-10: 99 rows naive, 24 rows with an explicit +00:00 offset, no other suffix seen). The cast strips any trailing Z/offset and reinterprets the remainder as UTC explicitly, so the result does not depend on the query session's timezone setting.

Coverage: 109 of 123 execution records join to neither workflow_metrics nor test_runs, and 312 of 330 learning_metrics rows have no metrics row. Neither dashboard joins those tables away — each counts its own spine — so those rows are in the numbers above. They are real runs, not pollution: the 109 cover 30 distinct queries across 9 domains with 62 passes, spanning 2026-02-23 to 2026-07-15; the 312 cover 30 distinct queries with 189 passes, spanning 2026-02-28 to 2026-07-15. What they blend is engine eras. The default now-1y window admits all of them, so narrowing the time picker is a deliberate act, not a floor this dashboard applies for you.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE test_status = 'passed') / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS pass_pct FROM execution_records WHERE (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()

SELECT test_status, count(*) AS runs FROM execution_records WHERE (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY runs DESC

panels.title: Failure categories
panels.description: Categories are also present on some passed rows, so this filters to failures explicitly rather than assuming a category implies a failure.

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(failure_category, '(none recorded)') AS category, count(*) AS failures, round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct FROM execution_records WHERE test_status <> 'passed' AND (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY failures DESC

SELECT failed_keyword, count(*) AS failures, count(DISTINCT domain) AS domains FROM execution_records WHERE test_status <> 'passed' AND failed_keyword IS NOT NULL AND (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY failures DESC

SELECT domain, count(*) AS runs, round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE test_status = 'passed') / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS pass_pct FROM execution_records WHERE (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY runs DESC

panels.title: Pass rate by generated code structure

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(code_structure, '(unclassified)') AS structure, count(*) AS runs, round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE test_status = 'passed') / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS pass_pct FROM execution_records WHERE (regexp_replace(timestamp, '(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:?[0-9]{2})$', '')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY runs DESC

panels.title: Aggregate error logs
panels.description: Errors from all three collected services, in the two formats they are actually written in. Arm A parses the structlog JSON the application emits and filters on its lowercase level field, which is what the Structured log level variable moves. Arm B is a literal ERROR substring match, which is the only way third-party loggers writing ANSI-coloured plain text are seen. Measured over 7 days on 2026-08-12: arm A 348 lines, arm B 58, overlap exactly 0 — dropping either arm loses a whole class of error. The shipped panel was arm B alone: 58 lines out of the combined 406, missing the 348 that only arm A catches. Both arms exclude one message, and it is the only thing either arm hides. LiteLLM logs 'Error creating standard logging object' on every LLM call, twice — once as ANSI plain text and once re-emitted as JSON — because its ordinary logging path imports a proxy-only module that this deployment does not install. Nothing in this repository reads the payload it fails to build, so the message reports no fault of ours and cannot be acted on. Re-measured on 2026-08-14 over the five days Loki actually holds: arm A 534 lines of which 90 were this message, arm B 90 lines of which all 90 were, so the exclusion leaves arm A at 444 real errors and arm B empty. Quote no window longer than the retained data: asking for seven days puts the range sample points outside it and silently returns fewer lines, not more. The absolute counts drift with traffic; the invariant is that arm B was entirely this one message, and that it lands twice per occurrence because it is written once as plain text and once as JSON. Arm B stays quiet until a genuine plain-text error appears — which is what an error panel should do when nothing is wrong. Arm B is kept for that case, not because it is catching anything today. Delete both exclusions once the upstream fix ships. level=critical currently matches 0 lines; it is in the pattern so the panel needs no edit when the first one appears, not because it is covering anything today. Arm B does not widen with the variable — it has no level field to filter on. Bench caveat: when the observability stack is running, a bench sweep targets the same containerised backend on 127.0.0.1:5000 that run_bench.py uses by default, so bench log lines land in this feed with no label separating them. Use the per-run log panel on the trace dashboard when you need certainty about which run a line belongs to.

targets.expr: {service=~"fastapi|browser-service|runner-exec"} != "Error creating standard logging object" | json | level=~"$level"
